findings.claim: Key Fact: Birling sacked Eva because she asked for a pay rise; “He saw this as ‘one of those cranks’ causing trouble.”
findings.truth: Birling never applies the word to Eva or to the strikers. His Act 1 line is “the way some of these cranks talk and write now, you’d think everybody has to look after everybody else” — aimed at people who preach community. “One of those cranks” is Eric’s phrase in Act 3 for the Inspector. Of Eva, Birling says she “had a lot to say — far too much — so she had to go.”
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1: “But the way some of these cranks talk and write now… community and all that nonsense”; Act 1: “except the four or five ringleaders… this girl, Eva Smith, was one of them, she’d had a lot to say — far too much — so she had to go”; Act 3 Eric: “and then one of those cranks walked in — the Inspector.” Full text: https://ormistonhorizonacademy.co.uk/admin/wp-content/uploads/sites/19/2023/03/An-Inspector-Calls-Play.pdf

findings.claim: Flashcard [10]: “What dismissive phrase does Birling use about strikers?” — “‘One of those cranks.’”
findings.truth: Same misattribution as F11. Birling’s real dismissal of the strikers is “If you don’t come down sharply on some of these people, they’d soon be asking for the earth.”
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1, Birling to the Inspector.

findings.claim: Flashcard [12]: “To whom does Birling show the photograph first?” — “Only himself — not to the others.”
findings.truth: The Inspector holds and shows the photograph; he shows it to Mr Birling alone. Birling shows it to nobody. The lesson’s own body text says so correctly.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1: the Inspector produces the photograph and “only allows BIRLING to see it”; Inspector: “One person and one line of inquiry at a time.”

findings.claim: Birling says the Chief Constable is “a friend of mine.”
findings.truth: The line is “he’s an old friend of mine”. A one-word truncation, not worth a live edit.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1: “Perhaps I ought to warn you that he’s an old friend of mine, and that I see him fairly frequently.”

findings.claim: “When Gerald ended the affair, he gave her money and ended the affair so he could focus on his business commitments” (clause duplicated, no full stop).
findings.truth: Gerald broke it off in the first week of September because he had to go away for several weeks on business, and insisted on giving Daisy a parting gift of money.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 2, Gerald: “In the first week of September. I had to go away for several weeks then — on business… So I broke it off definitely before I went”; “I insisted on a parting gift of enough money… to see her through to the end of the year.”

findings.claim: “Gerald notes early on that Eric is ‘squiffy’ (drunk).”
findings.truth: Sheila says it. “Squiffy” is Sheila’s word to her brother in Act 1; Eric later uses it of himself. Gerald’s remark about Eric’s drinking is a different line in Act 2 (“I have gathered that he does drink pretty hard”).
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1 — SHEILA: “You’re squiffy.” ERIC: “I’m not.” MRS BIRLING: “What an expression, Sheila!”

findings.claim: Flashcard [10]: “Alcoholism — Gerald noted he was often ‘squiffy.’”
findings.truth: Same misattribution as F16 — the speaker is Sheila.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1, Sheila to Eric.

findings.claim: Eric is quoted as saying “he’s been here and we all know what we did to her — and I say the girl’s dead.”
findings.truth: Fabricated. No such line exists. Eric’s Act 3 lines are “And I say the girl’s dead and we all helped to kill her — and that’s what matters” and, answering the hoax theory, “And it doesn’t alter the fact that we all helped to kill her.”
findings.evidence: Play text Act 3; searched the full text for “been here” — the only hit is Mrs Birling’s “I wish I’d been here when that man first arrived.”

findings.claim: Sheila is quoted as saying “It doesn’t make any difference — you know. Between us, we drove that girl to commit suicide — and that’s what matters.”
findings.truth: Only the middle clause is hers. Her real line is “Well, he inspected us all right. And don’t let’s start dodging and pretending now. Between us we drove that girl to commit suicide.” The phrase “It doesn’t make any difference” appears nowhere in the play, and “and that’s what matters” is Eric’s tag, not Sheila’s.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 3, Sheila (flaring up) after Birling says “He wasn’t an Inspector”; Eric (shouting): “And I say the girl’s dead and we all helped to kill her — and that’s what matters.”

findings.claim: Flashcard [5] carries the same spliced Sheila quotation with Eric’s tag attached.
findings.truth: Same as F19.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 3.

findings.claim: KC [2] stem: “Sheila says ‘It doesn’t make any difference’ because the Inspector’s _____ is irrelevant…”
findings.truth: The quoted phrase is invented (see F19). The answer key (‘identity’) is correct; only the stem needs the invented quotation removed.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 3.

findings.claim: “The family also rings the Infirmary to confirm no girl has died. They call the infirmary, which confirms no suicide has been admitted.”
findings.truth: The sentence is duplicated, and it is Gerald who telephones the Infirmary.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 3, Gerald: “By ringing up the Infirmary. Either there’s a dead girl there or there isn’t”, then “Brumley eight nine eight six… Is that the Infirmary?”

findings.claim: Eric is quoted as saying “he’s been here and we all know what we did.”
findings.truth: Fabricated — the same invented line as F18.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 3; the real line is “And I say the girl’s dead and we all helped to kill her — and that’s what matters.”

findings.claim: Key Fact: “Mrs Birling is the only character who never accepts any responsibility.”
findings.truth: Mr Birling never accepts responsibility either. He says “I can’t accept any responsibility” in Act 1 and is still calling the evening a joke at the end. Mrs Birling is the most defiant, not the only one.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1, Birling: “Still, I can’t accept any responsibility”; Act 3, Mrs Birling: “I was the only one of you who didn’t give in to him.”

findings.claim: Birling is quoted as saying “a man has to look after himself.”
findings.truth: Not a contiguous quotation. The line is “a man has to mind his own business and look after himself and his own”.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1, Birling’s speech immediately before the doorbell.

findings.claim: Flashcard [2] repeats the same non-verbatim quotation.
findings.truth: Same as F25.
findings.evidence: Play text Act 1.

findings.claim: The Inspector is quoted as saying “I’m not here to talk about your knighthood.”
findings.truth: Fabricated. The Inspector never mentions the knighthood; only Birling and Eric do. His short deflating replies are “(dryly) I don’t play golf” (to Birling name-dropping the Chief Constable) and “(massively) Public men, Mr Birling, have responsibilities as well as privileges.”
findings.evidence: Searched the full text for “knighthood” — four hits, all Birling or Eric, none the Inspector. Play text Acts 1 and 2.

findings.claim: Flashcard [2] asks what the Inspector says about the knighthood and answers with the fabricated line.
findings.truth: Same as F27; replaced with “Public men, Mr Birling, have responsibilities as well as privileges.”
findings.evidence: Play text Act 2, after Birling says “I’m a public man—”.

summary: Every lesson carried the same two exam-format faults: a Paper 1 style extract question and one or two practice questions labelled “Shakespeare Essay” on a Paper 2 modern-text unit. On top of that, five fabricated or misattributed quotations were found (Eric's Act 3 line invented twice, Sheila's Act 3 line spliced with Eric's tag, the Inspector's 'knighthood' line invented, and 'squiffy' credited to Gerald instead of Sheila), plus a misapplied 'cranks' quotation and one false uniqueness claim about Mrs Birling. 40 edits, all validated against the live rows.
